proof:
# Fixed global mass does not give moment-body volume payment

Let B_t(j) denote the body of continuous barycenters of dominated
mass-t submeasures whose integer barycenter is j. The proposed stronger
comparison

    mu(H) >= t vol_d(B_t(j) intersect H_j)/vol_d(B_t(j))       (1)

fails even at t=M/2^n and at an integer base satisfying D_j>=t.
Here H_j is the slice of the ambient halfspace at base j.

## 1. Exact cubical counterexample in every n,d>=1

For d>=1 set

    K_0=[0,1]^d,
    K_1=[0,4/5] times [0,1]^(d-1).

Take the convex hull of these two fibers in the first integer
coordinate, and take its product with [0,1]^(n-1) in the remaining
integer coordinates. All sampled bases are the vertices of [0,1]^n.
Their continuous fibers equal K_0 or K_1 according to the first bit.

Their total mixed volume is

    M=2^(n-1)(1+4/5)=2^n (9/10),
    t=M/2^n=9/10.

At j=0 every integer coordinate is nonnegative. The zero base-moment
constraint forces the entire selected measure into K_0. Thus B_t(j)
is the usual mass-9/10 moment body of the unit cube.

The exact lower x_1 support value of this body is9/20, attained by
the bottom slab 0<=x_1<=9/10. The threshold exchange inequality
proves optimality. Hence the halfspace

    H={x_1-2 sum_(i=1)^n z_i >=9/20}

contains the WHOLE moment body above j. It excludes all other integer
fibers, because at any nonzero base its threshold is at least49/20>1.
Consequently

    mu(H)=11/20 <9/10=t.                             (2)

The moment body has positive d-volume. For example the densities

    f(x)=9/10 + sum_i a_i(2x_i-1),
    sum_i |a_i|<1/10,

are feasible in the cube, all have mass9/10, and their barycenters
vary with independent nonzero derivatives in every coordinate.

Also D_j=1: every base halfspace containing j includes its unit-volume
fiber, and a halfspace with a sufficiently negative sum of integer
coordinates isolates it. Thus D_j>=t. Equations (1)--(2) disprove the
comparison under exactly that mass and base-depth requirement.

## 2. No universal coefficient larger than gamma_d can repair (1)

For an exact limiting obstruction, replace K_0 by the standard
d-simplex Delta of volume V=1/d!, and let

    K_1=(1-2delta)^(1/d) Delta,   0<delta<1/2.

Use the same n-dimensional cube of integer bases. Then

    M=2^n(1-delta)V,    t=(1-delta)V,
    D_0=V>=t.

Again all selected mass at base0 must lie in Delta. Write alpha=1-delta.
For a uniform point of Delta, the x_1 marginal has tail probability
(1-c)^d and mean1/(d+1). The top delta-volume portion has mean

    1 - [d/(d+1)] delta^(1/d).

By taking the complement, the smallest x_1 barycenter of a selected
alpha-volume portion is therefore

    c_delta=[1/(d+1)-delta
                   +(d/(d+1))delta^(1+1/d)]/(1-delta).       (3)

Top/bottom threshold exchange proves these extrema exactly. In
particular B_t(0) lies in {x_1>=c_delta}. It is full dimensional:
bounded small zero-mean affine perturbations of the constant density
alpha give independent first-moment variations, since the simplex
covariance matrix is positive definite.

Extend {x_1>=c_delta} by a finite integer tilt excluding all other
cube vertices. The resulting ambient halfspace contains the entire
moment body and has mixed measure

    V(1-c_delta)^d.

Its ratio to t is exactly

    gamma_d (1-delta^(1+1/d))^d/(1-delta)^(d+1),             (4)

where gamma_d=(d/(d+1))^d. This tends to gamma_d as delta decreases
to zero.

Thus any universally valid replacement of (1) by

    mu(H) >= c_d t vol(B_t(j) intersect H_j)/vol(B_t(j))

must have c_d<=gamma_d. Applying ordinary Grunbaum to B_t after such
a scalar comparison would at best pay another gamma_d and would not
recover the desired single gamma_d factor by that mechanism.

This is a limitation of that volume-comparison route, not a proof
that the weakened comparison with c_d=gamma_d is valid.

The simplex moment body itself is invariant under every affine vertex
permutation of Delta; its centroid is consequently the simplex
centroid. Hence this family does not refute the moment-body-centroid
selector. The separate padding note does refute that selector for
an arbitrary Doignon-qualified base.
